title: Acts Chapter 27 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 27 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 27 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 27.

questions.question: In Acts 27, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: They sailed under Cyprus because the winds were contrary
Paul was delivered to Julius, a centurion
Paul admonished that the voyage would be with hurt and much damage
questions.correctAnswer: Paul was delivered to Julius, a centurion
questions.explanation: Acts 27:1 states that Paul and other prisoners were delivered to Julius before any sailing or admonitions.

questions.question: Who was the centurion assigned to Paul and the other prisoners?
questions.correctAnswer: Julius
questions.explanation: Acts 27:1 states that Paul and others were delivered to Julius, a centurion of Augustus' band.

questions.question: From which city did the ship that they boarded at the start of the voyage come?
questions.correctAnswer: Adramyttium
questions.explanation: Acts 27:2 says they entered into a ship of Adramyttium.

questions.question: Who was the Macedonian from Thessalonica that was with them?
questions.correctAnswer: Aristarchus
questions.explanation: Acts 27:2 states that Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, was with them.

questions.question: Where did the ship touch the next day, and what did Julius allow Paul to do there?
options: Sidon; Paul was allowed to visit his friends to refresh himself
Myra; Paul was allowed to rest on the shore
Lasea; Paul was allowed to preach
Cnidus; Paul was allowed to pray
questions.correctAnswer: Sidon; Paul was allowed to visit his friends to refresh himself
questions.explanation: Acts 27:3 states that they touched at Sidon, and Julius courteously entreated Paul and gave him liberty to go to his friends to refresh himself.

questions.question: Why did they sail under Cyprus after leaving Sidon?
questions.correctAnswer: Because the winds were contrary
questions.explanation: Acts 27:4 states they sailed under Cyprus because the winds were contrary.

questions.question: At which city of Lycia did they arrive after sailing over the seas of Cilicia and Pamphylia?
questions.correctAnswer: Myra
questions.explanation: Acts 27:5 says they came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

questions.question: What type of ship did the centurion find at Myra, and where was it sailing?
options: A ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy
A ship of Thessalonica sailing to Cyprus
A ship of Crete sailing to Sidon
A ship of Lasea sailing to Myra
questions.correctAnswer: A ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy
questions.explanation: Acts 27:6 states the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy and put them in it.

questions.question: Where did they sail after being caught by a wind that did not allow them to pass Cnidus?
questions.correctAnswer: Under Crete, over against Salmone
questions.explanation: Acts 27:7 states that when they could not pass Cnidus because of the wind, they sailed under Crete, over against Salmone.

questions.question: What is the name of the place called 'The fair havens' near the city of Lasea?
options: A place where they came after hardly passing Salmone
questions.correctAnswer: A place where they came after hardly passing Salmone
questions.explanation: Acts 27:8 says they came to a place called The fair havens, near Lasea, after passing Salmone.

questions.question: Why did Paul admonish the crew about the voyage at The fair havens?
options: Because the voyage would be with hurt and much damage to the ship, lading, and lives
Because they should sail immediately to Alexandria
questions.correctAnswer: Because the voyage would be with hurt and much damage to the ship, lading, and lives
questions.explanation: Acts 27:10 shows Paul said the voyage would be with hurt and much damage, not only to the ship and cargo but also to their lives.

questions.question: Who did the centurion believe more than Paul's warning?
options: The master and the owner of the ship
questions.correctAnswer: The master and the owner of the ship
questions.explanation: Acts 27:11 states the centurion believed the master and ship owner more than Paul's words.

questions.question: Why did the majority advise to depart from The fair havens to Phenice?
options: Because The fair havens was not commodious to winter in
Because Phenice was a city of Lycia
questions.correctAnswer: Because The fair havens was not commodious to winter in
questions.explanation: Acts 27:12 says the majority advised departure because The fair havens was not suitable to winter in.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was given liberty by Julius to visit his friends at Sidon.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 27:3 states Julius courteously entreated Paul and gave him liberty to visit his friends.

questions.question: True or False: The ship was caught in a tempestuous wind called Euroclydon.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 27:14 mentions the tempestuous wind called Euroclydon arose against them.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 27 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 27 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the shipmen do to prevent the ship from falling into quicksands?
options: They cast out the tackling of the ship
questions.correctAnswer: They undergirded the ship
questions.explanation: They used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven. (Acts 27:17)

questions.question: What does Acts 27:22 promise will happen if someone does what Acts 27:21 commands?
options: They will be saved from the storm
No loss of life will occur
questions.correctAnswer: No loss of life will occur
questions.explanation: Paul exhorts them to be of good cheer, for there shall be no loss of any man's life among you, but of the ship. (Acts 27:22)

questions.question: What action did the crew take on the third day to lighten the ship?
options: They cast out the tackling of the ship
questions.correctAnswer: They cast out the tackling of the ship
questions.explanation: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship. (Acts 27:19)

questions.question: What does Acts 27:20 indicate about the condition of the voyage?
options: They had lost all hope of being saved
The sun appeared after many days
questions.correctAnswer: They had lost all hope of being saved
questions.explanation: All hope that we should be saved was then taken away. (Acts 27:20)

questions.question: What did Paul say after long abstinence?
options: We should have listened to him
questions.correctAnswer: We should have listened to him
questions.explanation: Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete. (Acts 27:21)

questions.question: What did the angel of God assure Paul about those sailing with him?
questions.correctAnswer: They would be safe
questions.explanation: God hath given thee all them that sail with thee. (Acts 27:24)

questions.question: What did Paul express confidence in regarding God's message?
options: It shall be as he believed
They would be lost at sea
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be as he believed
questions.explanation: For I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me. (Acts 27:25)

questions.question: What was the depth of the water when they sounded and found it twenty fathoms?
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty fathoms
questions.explanation: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms. (Acts 27:28)

questions.question: What did the crew do when they feared they would fall upon rocks?
questions.correctAnswer: They cast out anchors
questions.explanation: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern. (Acts 27:29)

questions.question: What were the shipmen planning to do when they let down the boat into the sea?
questions.correctAnswer: Escape the ship
questions.explanation: As the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea. (Acts 27:30)

questions.question: What was the primary reason Paul advised against leaving Crete?
questions.correctAnswer: He foresaw danger and damage
questions.explanation: Paul admonished them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage. (Acts 27:10)

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'fourteenth night' mentioned in Acts 27:27?
options: They had been lost at sea for fourteen days
They had been in a storm for fourteen days
It was a time of prayer
questions.correctAnswer: They had been in a storm for fourteen days
questions.explanation: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria. (Acts 27:27)

questions.question: Was it true that Paul was promised he would reach Caesar?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The angel told Paul, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar. (Acts 27:24)

questions.question: Did the crew initially believe Paul's warning about the voyage's danger?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul. (Acts 27:11)

questions.question: Was Paul confident that they would perish in the storm?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Paul expressed belief that there would be no loss of life among them. (Acts 27:22)

hard.title: Acts Chapter 27 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 27.

questions.question: In Acts 27:31, what did Paul say was necessary for salvation during the shipwreck?
options: Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.
Throw all cargo overboard to lighten the ship.
Swim to the shore as fast as possible.
questions.correctAnswer: Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.
questions.explanation: Acts 27:31 records Paul telling the centurion and soldiers that staying in the ship was necessary for salvation.

questions.question: According to Acts 27:32, how did the soldiers prevent the ship's boat from being used to escape?
options: They cut off the ropes of the boat and let her fall off.
They tied the boat securely to the ship.
They sank the boat in the sea.
They locked the boat in the ship's hold.
questions.correctAnswer: They cut off the ropes of the boat and let her fall off.
questions.explanation: Acts 27:32 states the soldiers cut the ropes of the boat and let it fall off to prevent escape.

questions.question: In Acts 27:33-34, why did Paul urge the ship's company to take meat after fasting for fourteen days?
options: For their health, so that no hair would fall from their heads.
To prepare them for the upcoming battle with the sea.
Because the ship was approaching land and they needed strength.
To offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving to God.
questions.correctAnswer: For their health, so that no hair would fall from their heads.
questions.explanation: Paul encouraged them to eat for health reasons, promising no hair would fall from any of them (Acts 27:33-34).

questions.question: What did Paul do in Acts 27:35 before eating bread with all on the ship?
options: Gave thanks to God in presence of them all.
questions.correctAnswer: Gave thanks to God in presence of them all.
questions.explanation: Acts 27:35 describes Paul giving thanks to God publicly before breaking and eating the bread.

questions.question: How many souls were aboard the ship according to Acts 27:37?
options: Two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
questions.correctAnswer: Two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
questions.explanation: Acts 27:37 states that there were 276 souls aboard the ship.

questions.question: What action did the crew take after they had eaten enough in Acts 27:38?
options: They lightened the ship by casting out the wheat into the sea.
They prepared the lifeboats for evacuation.
They raised a flag signaling for help.
They anchored near the shore to rest.
questions.correctAnswer: They lightened the ship by casting out the wheat into the sea.
questions.explanation: Acts 27:38 says they lightened the ship by throwing the wheat overboard after eating.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'abide' (μένω) used in Acts 27:31 most closely mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To remain or stay continuously
questions.explanation: In Acts 27:31, the Greek verb 'μένω' (meno) means to remain or stay continuously, emphasizing the necessity to stay in the ship for salvation.

questions.question: Which literary device is exemplified in Acts 27:41 where the ship runs aground 'where two seas met'?
questions.correctAnswer: Typology
questions.explanation: The meeting of two seas and the ship running aground in Acts 27:41 can be seen as typology, symbolizing the struggle and salvation motif found throughout Scripture.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of protection and deliverance in Acts 27:23-24, where an angel assures Paul he will be saved?
questions.explanation: Psalm 91:11-12 speaks of angels guarding the faithful, paralleling the angel's assurance to Paul in Acts 27:23-24.

questions.question: Which New Testament event fulfills the theme of shipwreck and divine preservation found in Acts 27?
options: Paul's conversion on the road to Damascus (Acts 9:1-19)
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus calming the storm (Mark 4:35-41)
questions.explanation: Mark 4:35-41 features Jesus calming a storm, echoing the theme of divine protection during perilous sea conditions like in Acts 27.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Paul's instruction not to abandon ship in Acts 27:31?
options: The shipmen attempt to flee by lowering the boat into the sea.
The crew casts lots to decide their fate.
Paul breaks bread and gives thanks.
The centurion orders the anchors to be dropped.
questions.correctAnswer: The shipmen attempt to flee by lowering the boat into the sea.
questions.explanation: Acts 27:30 describes the shipmen trying to escape by lowering the boat before Paul commands to stay in the ship in verse 31.

questions.question: How does the literary device of inclusio appear in the narrative of Acts 27?
options: The narrative begins and ends with Paul's assurance of safety.
Repeated references to the number of souls aboard the ship.
Use of repeated nautical terms to frame the story.
questions.correctAnswer: The narrative begins and ends with Paul's assurance of safety.
questions.explanation: Acts 27 forms an inclusio by opening with Paul's warning and ending with the safe landing of all, emphasizing God's preservation (Acts 27:22 and 27:44).

questions.question: What is the significance of the number of days fasting mentioned in Acts 27:33 in the context of Jewish tradition?
options: Fourteen days relates to the Passover preparation period.
Fourteen days correspond to the Feast of Tabernacles.
Fourteen days signify a purification ritual.
Fourteen days is the standard mourning period.
questions.correctAnswer: Fourteen days relates to the Passover preparation period.
questions.explanation: The fourteen days fasting (Acts 27:33) corresponds to the Jewish tradition of preparation for Passover, symbolizing trial before deliverance.

questions.question: How does the Greek term for 'lightened' (ἐλαφρύνοντες) in Acts 27:38 reflect a maritime practice?
options: Reducing the ship's weight by throwing cargo overboard.
Raising sails to catch more wind.
Securing the anchors to stabilize the ship.
Reinforcing the hull to withstand waves.
questions.correctAnswer: Reducing the ship's weight by throwing cargo overboard.
questions.explanation: The Greek word ἐλαφρύνοντες in Acts 27:38 means to make lighter, a common maritime practice to improve buoyancy in storms by discarding cargo.

questions.question: True or False: According to Acts 27:44, all aboard the ship perished in the shipwreck.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 27:44 clearly states that all escaped safely to land, so the statement is false.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 27 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 27 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 27:10 teach about human sin and divine providence?
options: Human disobedience can lead to physical harm despite God's overarching plan
God punishes all sinners immediately with physical calamities
Faith always guarantees physical safety regardless of circumstances
Humans have no responsibility in events ordained by God
questions.correctAnswer: Human disobedience can lead to physical harm despite God's overarching plan
questions.explanation: Acts 27:10 shows Paul warning that the voyage will result in damage and loss of life, indicating human choices affect outcomes even under God’s sovereign plan.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 27:23-24 teach about God's providential guidance and protection of believers?
options: God sends angels to reassure and protect His servants in trials
Believers are exempt from all dangers and suffering
God’s providence is limited to spiritual matters only
Human effort alone determines survival in perilous situations
questions.correctAnswer: God sends angels to reassure and protect His servants in trials
questions.explanation: Acts 27:23-24 records an angel assuring Paul that God has granted safety to all aboard, demonstrating divine intervention and care.

questions.question: What doctrine about salvation does Acts 27:22 teach?
options: Salvation of life is assured by God’s promise despite physical loss
Salvation requires perfect adherence to all instructions without fail
Salvation is conditional solely on human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation of life is assured by God’s promise despite physical loss
questions.explanation: Acts 27:22 has Paul exhorting the crew that no life will be lost, though the ship will be lost, illustrating spiritual salvation over physical preservation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 27:24 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Acts 27:24 shows God's sovereign control over Paul's fate and those sailing with him, directing events to fulfill His purposes.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 27:35 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: In Acts 27:35, Paul giving thanks before breaking bread shows God's providential provision and care even in dire circumstances.

questions.question: How does the shipwreck in Acts 27 connect to the broader biblical theme of God's deliverance of His people?
options: It prefigures God’s saving of Israel through the Red Sea crossing
It contradicts the Old Testament theme of divine protection
It shows that God abandons sinners in danger
It illustrates human self-salvation without divine help
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures God’s saving of Israel through the Red Sea crossing
questions.explanation: Acts 27’s shipwreck and salvation echo God’s deliverance of Israel from peril, demonstrating continuity in God’s saving acts (cf. Exodus 14).

questions.question: How does Paul’s assurance to the sailors in Acts 27:22-25 fulfill the theme of Christ’s victory over death and fear elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It anticipates the resurrection hope that overcomes fear of death
It denies the reality of danger or death
It teaches that faith eliminates all human suffering
It emphasizes avoidance of all trials through prayer
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the resurrection hope that overcomes fear of death
questions.explanation: Paul’s encouragement to be of good cheer because no life will perish (Acts 27:22-25) reflects the hope in Christ’s victory over death (cf. 1 Corinthians 15).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 27:23 and Acts 27:24 teach about God's providence and angelic ministry?
options: God sovereignly appoints angels to protect and guide His servants
Angels act independently from God's will
Angelic protection guarantees exemption from all harm
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly appoints angels to protect and guide His servants
questions.explanation: Acts 27:23-24 shows an angel speaking to Paul by God’s authority, illustrating divine providence using angelic agents.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 27:10 and Acts 27:21 reveal about human responsibility and divine warning through prophecy?
options: God warns through prophetic messages but humans retain responsibility to heed warnings
Warnings from God are optional and have no real effect
questions.correctAnswer: God warns through prophetic messages but humans retain responsibility to heed warnings
questions.explanation: Paul’s warnings in Acts 27:10 and 27:21 show that God’s prophetic word calls for human obedience, blending divine foreknowledge and human responsibility.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 27:37 and Acts 27:44 teach about corporate salvation and God’s faithfulness to all in the community of believers?
options: God’s salvation extends to the entire community under His care
Only the spiritually perfect are saved in group crises
Salvation is an individual matter unrelated to the community
God’s promises do not guarantee physical preservation
questions.correctAnswer: God’s salvation extends to the entire community under His care
questions.explanation: Acts 27:37 and 27:44 show all 276 aboard survived, illustrating God’s faithfulness to the entire group, not just individuals.

questions.question: Skeptics claim the shipwreck in Acts 27:14-44 shows that God is indifferent to human suffering and does not intervene. What does Acts 27:23-24 actually teach?
options: God actively intervenes through His angel to assure safety for Paul and those with him
God abandons people in physical dangers to test their faith
The shipwreck was purely natural without divine involvement
God’s intervention guarantees no harm or loss of property
questions.correctAnswer: God actively intervenes through His angel to assure safety for Paul and those with him
questions.explanation: Acts 27:23-24 depicts an angel sent by God reassuring Paul of divine protection, showing God’s involved care despite the storm.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 27:12 teach about human wisdom and discernment in relation to God's providence?
options: Human prudence can guide decisions but does not override God’s sovereign will
Human judgment is always superior to divine guidance
God’s providence negates the need for human planning
Humans must ignore circumstances entirely to trust God
questions.correctAnswer: Human prudence can guide decisions but does not override God’s sovereign will
questions.explanation: Acts 27:12 shows the crew choosing a better harbor to winter in, indicating human judgment operates within God’s providential framework.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 27:26 specifically demonstrate when stating 'we must be cast upon a certain island'?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Acts 27:26 reveals God's sovereign control over the ship’s destiny, determining where they must land despite human efforts.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 27:33-35 and Acts 27:36 teach about faith and the practice of worship amid trials?
options: Faith expressed through thanksgiving sustains believers and encourages community in adversity
Worship is only appropriate in times of peace
Faith eliminates the need for physical nourishment
Thanksgiving is a private act unrelated to communal encouragement
questions.correctAnswer: Faith expressed through thanksgiving sustains believers and encourages community in adversity
questions.explanation: Paul’s giving thanks and breaking bread (Acts 27:33-35) followed by communal eating (Acts 27:36) shows worship’s role in sustaining faith amid crisis.

questions.question: How does Acts 27:42-43 demonstrate the theme of divine intervention in human affairs as seen throughout Scripture?
options: God uses human agents (the centurion) to prevent injustice and preserve life
God is passive and allows evil to succeed
Divine intervention always overrides human free will immediately
God prefers destruction over mercy in judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God uses human agents (the centurion) to prevent injustice and preserve life
questions.explanation: The centurion’s action in Acts 27:42-43 to save the prisoners reflects God’s providential use of human agents to accomplish His purposes.
